newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities creep up ahead of G7.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities creep up ahead of G7.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options crept up in U.S. business as the market awaited Sunday's Group of Seven meeting, dealers said.

"There's a lot of nervousness the dollar's going to move four big figures (pfennigs) one way or the other like it did the last time (after the February G7 meeting)," said Ted Voorhees, a senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York.
"Until very recently everyone was just bullish on the dollar, but G7 has stirred things up particularly in dollar/yen," added Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York.
Shorter-dated options were well bid in most currencies, although few traders expected the G7 to take drastic measures on exchange rates or mention specific levels in their communique.
One-week dollar/yen volatility rose more than a full point on the day to about 10.5/11.5 percent, while one-month gained more than a quarter point to 9.2/9.4 percent.

Hiramatsu said the movement in spot dollar, which ranged between 125.50-126.35 yen today, was enough for a delta-hedger to justify the relatively rich one-week premium, provided the trader was able to capture most of the width in spot.

Risk reversals, the cost of swapping equally out-of-the- money puts and calls, stayed skewed toward yen calls in the front end and around par in the back end. One-month 25-delta was steady at 0.1/0.4 point in favor of yen calls.

While fundamentals supported the dollar in the longer term, many traders expected the greenback to come under pressure for a while as the market second-guesses what agreements might have taken place at the G7 meeting.
Dollar/mark volatilities were also firmer across the board, along with dollar/Swiss.
A European bank trader in New York said a large U.S. investment bank was a big buyer of one-year dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss franc options.
One-year dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss stood at 9.25/9.45 and 11.0/11.2 percent respectively, up about 0.2 point each. One-month dollar/mark rose 0.3 to 9.0/9.2 percent.

In contrast to the increasingly mixed outlook for dollar/yen due to U.S.-Japan trade imbalances, most traders focused on the dollar's upside risk against European currencies, with strike prices up to 1.80 marks commonly trading even in the shorter maturities, traders said.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal for dollar/mark was steady at 0.1/0.3 point in favor of mark puts.
Sterling volatilities were slightly softer despite the upcoming U.K. general elections on May 1.
"A lot of people have already become long sterling volatilities and some probably needed time-decay adjustment," Hiramatsu at Bank of Yokohama said.
One-month cable was off about 0.2 point at about 7.0/7.3 percent.
